subtitulo: The verb-noun pairs native speakers never choose consciously
descripcion: Collocation is where advanced learners are exposed most reliably. Grammar correct, vocabulary wide, and then they *make* a decision instead of *taking* one, or *do* research instead of *conducting* it. There is no rule; the pairings are conventional and must be learned as pairs. It is the highest-return vocabulary work at C1, because the individual words are already known.

ejemplos.texto: *We'd need to draw a distinction between liquidity and solvency before answering that.*
*She took out a policy that satisfies the conditions but doesn't meet the requirement.*
*The employer bears the cost; the employee absorbs the risk.*
*I'd want to raise a concern before we commit to that.*
*They conducted the analysis but never reached a conclusion.*

notas: Verb-noun is the highest-value pattern; adjective-noun (*a compelling case*, *a marked increase*) is second.
British and American collocations diverge more than vocabulary does. Pick one and be consistent.
Synonyms do not collocate alike: *a strong argument* is fine, *a forceful argument* means something else.

contraste.es: Spanish has one verb (*hacer*) where English splits into *do*, *make*, *take*, *draw* and *carry out*. That single mismatch generates most collocation errors by Spanish speakers.
contraste.de: German machen covers both do and make (Hausaufgaben machen – do homework, einen Fehler machen – make a mistake), so German speakers face the same split. Some German collocations help: eine Schlussfolgerung ziehen – draw a conclusion.
contraste.it: Italian fare covers do and make (fare i compiti – do homework, fare un errore – make a mistake), and even ask a question (fare una domanda). The English split has to be learned pair by pair.
contraste.fr: French faire covers do and make (faire ses devoirs – do homework, faire une erreur – make a mistake). Some collocations help: tirer une conclusion – draw a conclusion.
contraste.pt: Portuguese fazer covers do and make (fazer os trabalhos de casa – do homework, fazer um erro – make a mistake) and even ask (fazer uma pergunta). The English split has to be learned pair by pair.

errores: *make a research*, *do a decision*, *make an exam*.
Defaulting to *do* and *make* whenever the precise verb does not surface fast enough.

es: *realizar una presentación* rendered as *realise a presentation* instead of *give a presentation*.
de: *einen Vortrag halten* rendered as *hold a talk* instead of *give a talk*.
it: *tenere una conferenza* rendered as *hold a conference* instead of *give a talk* or *give a lecture*.
fr: *faire une conférence* rendered as *make a conference* instead of *give a lecture*.
pt: *assistir a uma reunião* rendered as *assist a meeting* instead of *attend a meeting*.

traducciones.it: accendere un prestito / stipulare una polizza
traducciones.pt: contrair um empréstimo / fazer um seguro

traducciones.es: vivir por encima de tus posibilidades
traducciones.it: vivere al di sopra delle proprie possibilità

mision.consigna: Explain how a pension or insurance system works to someone who is not from here.
requisitos: no *do* or *make* where a more precise verb exists

microtareas.texto: Write ten nouns you use at work and find the conventional verb for each.
Rewrite four sentences replacing every *do* and *make* with a precise verb.
Record 90 seconds explaining a financial product. Count your collocations.

autochequeo: Any surviving *do* or *make* a native would replace?
Any synonym swapped in that breaks the collocation?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on collocation. (1) Mark every verb-noun pair; where mine is wrong, give the conventional one. (2) Flag every *do*/*make* a native would replace. (3) Flag BrE/AmE inconsistency. (4) Give five collocations I should have used on this topic and didn't. Do not rewrite the text.
